## Yamaha Serial 0.2.0

First public release. The component is `beta`: the protocol layer and the
entity model are stable, hardware validation across receiver families is not.

### What this gives you

A native ESPHome external component for Yamaha RS-232 receivers, with a
non-blocking UART parser, a command queue with spacing, timeouts and retries,
and ESPHome-native entities instead of a template-and-script construction.

- One `media_player` entity for daily control: power, mute, volume, volume
  step, next/previous DSP program
- `select` entities for input source and DSP program, plus Zone2, tuner,
  sleep timer, decoder and speaker controls
- Extended setup controls (bass, treble, speaker distances, dimmer) on
  RX-Vx600-style receivers
- Diagnostics that make a support report decidable: connection state, last
  error, last parse error with the rejected frame, response age and counters
- A raw command action with symbolic aliases, so model-specific functions stay
  reachable without carrying hex payloads in automations

### Receiver profiles

Standard and extended profiles for the RX-Vx500, RX-Vx600, RX-Vx700 and
RX-Vx800 families. With `receiver_profile: auto` the `model` hint starts the
session and the matching extended profile is reapplied once the receiver
reports its real model, keeping your configured input labels.

### Source and sound mode in Home Assistant

ESPHome's media-player call path still carries no source or sound-mode value,
so the ESPHome entity deliberately does not advertise those flags. If you want
one native receiver `media_player` with `source_list`, `sound_mode_list`,
`select_source` and `select_sound_mode`, install the optional Home Assistant
companion integration shipped in this repository. See
[SUPPORT.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/SUPPORT.md) for the detail and
[docs/home_assistant_companion.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/docs/home_assistant_companion.md) for
the setup.

### Before you wire anything

Yamaha DB9 ports carry true RS-232 levels, not 3.3V TTL. A direct GPIO
connection can destroy the ESP, the receiver port, or both. Use a MAX3232-class
level converter: [docs/wiring.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/docs/wiring.md).

### Installation

```yaml
external_components:
  - source: github://memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial@v0.2.0
    components: [yamaha_serial]
```

Requires ESPHome 2026.9.0 or newer. Start from
[examples/yamaha_rx_v_basic.yaml](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/examples/yamaha_rx_v_basic.yaml).

### Known limitations

- No receiver model is claimed as fully hardware-validated across the whole
  command surface. Reports from untested models are welcome.
- x700 and x800 profile maps need broader hardware validation.
- Zone2 report behaviour varies by model and firmware.
- Region-specific XM/NET/USB blocks differ across models.

The full changelog is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/memphi2/ESPHome-Yamaha-Serial/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
